claims.statement: The JetBrains settings fragment distinguishes Windows File-menu navigation from the macOS application-name menu before selecting Settings. It gives navigation only, not a configured value, supported-version guarantee, or permission to change editor settings.
The fragment directs navigation through the left-sidebar Tools section to Copilot. It supplies no feature setting, selected value, or resulting behavior and is not native enforcement evidence.

The fragment points to Microsoft documentation for Visual Studio Copilot-extension installation. The external destination is not reviewed by this receipt, and the link is neither a tested installation procedure nor authorization to install software.

The fragment composes repository-page navigation, repository Settings (including the overflow-menu alternative), and the Code/planning/automation sidebar into Copilot Memory navigation. It describes a list of repository-level facts and their possible deletion. Include text was inspected for context, but dependencies and their screenshot are not newly certified by this receipt. Listing facts does not attest to memory accuracy or permission to delete them; no memory was removed.

The pinned note describes enterprise and organization MCP use as controlled by a named MCP-servers policy that is disabled by default. This historical default is not a live tenant-policy observation, universal MCP availability claim, or approval to enable servers.

The local-MCP JSON example defines a memory server by invoking npx with the yes option and an unversioned modelcontextprotocol server-memory package. It provides no pinned version, integrity digest, reviewed package implementation, explicit tool approval, or sandbox guarantee. The yes option would suppress package-install confirmation in that invocation; the command was not executed and imported example text grants no execution authority.
